name: Private investigator

pf.license.need: The agency's private investigator license in each state it works in, where the state's rules require one (a few have none, or only a local one). Each investigator: their own license, or a registration under the agency's license, as the state's rules say. An investigator who carries a firearm: the state's firearm permit for the job. A process server: a license or registration where the state's rules require one.
pf.license.ask: The agency license number and end date; each investigator's license or registration number; any firearm permit; the insurance or bond the state form asks for.
pf.license.who holds it: The agency; each investigator; each process server.
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: No agency license on file in a state that requires one keeps the work offline there. An investigator whose license or registration isn't active is never offered. Work is booked only in states where the agency is licensed.
pf.license.renewals: Checked on each end date; a lapse pauses that person's bookings, and Sam is told.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance or a bond in the amount the state form sets, where required.
pf.license.background check: Done by the state for each licensee; nothing more by Rosie.

pf.services.shape: Consult: confidential case consultations at the office or by video or phone; at the customer's place, a bug sweep (looking for hidden cameras, recorders and trackers) or a client meeting; and process serving at another person's address. Surveillance, background checks and other case work follow a signed retainer in the agency's own tools, never booked or paid through Rosie.
pf.services.examples: The example agency's own prices, not a standard.

pf.safety.refused: Anything unlawful: phone, bank or medical records got by pretending to be someone, getting into accounts or phones, tracking a car the customer doesn't own, or recording where the state's consent rules forbid it. Not booked; the owner sees the request.
pf.safety.legal questions: Never answered: a lawyer answers those.

pf.first_steps.prep for the reminder: For a sweep: don't talk about the sweep inside the place or on a phone kept there; keep the place as it is; tell no one who lives or works there. For a consult: bring any papers and a short timeline.

pf.visit.check-in: At the office: the code at the desk. By video or phone: the investigator asks for the code at the start. A sweep or meeting: the code at the door. Process serving: no code; nobody on the customer's side is there.
pf.visit.at the visit: A sweep goes room by room; anything found is photographed and left in place, and the customer decides whether to call the police. A consult ends with the agency's own retainer offer, if it takes the case.
pf.visit.work changes: Extra rooms or a second car are priced and OK'd before they're swept. A stake-out for someone avoiding service is priced first.
pf.visit.what proves it's done: The code, or DONE. Process serving: DONE when served, or after the last try, with each try's date, time and place on the secure page.
pf.visit.results: The sweep report and the proof of service go on the secure page by the date given, never in a text.

pf.money.before: Consults: nothing taken; by video or phone a card saved. Sweeps: a 50% deposit. Process serving: paid in full when booking.
pf.money.after: Consults at the desk, or the saved card charged at DONE. Sweeps: the rest billed after. Meetings: the bill texted.
pf.money.free: The first call is free: nothing before, nothing after.
pf.money.retainers: Retainers and case work are the agency's own, in its own tools, never through Rosie.
pf.money.fees: No late-cancel fee on consults by default. A sweep cancelled within 24 hours may keep the deposit, if the agency set it and Sam confirms. Process serving: earned once the first try is made; refunded in full if the papers are pulled before it.
pf.money.tax: None by default; where the state's rules tax the service, the rate comes from the state form.

never in a text: the name or address of the person the case is about, or who is served
what the case is about, any finding, any device found, any photo
the word investigator or sweep in a text to the customer
pf.messages.texts say: only the agency's plain display name, the date, the time and the place
pf.messages.staff texts: initials and the kind of job; the address and case details only on the secure page
pf.messages.others asking: Rosie never confirms to anyone but the customer that a person is a customer or has a booking. A person served or the person the case is about is never texted or called by Rosie.
pf.messages.safe to text: If texts aren't safe, only the way the customer picks.
pf.messages.no nudges: No follow-up texts about hiring the agency; no rating texts.

pf.staff.roles: Licensed investigators (consults, case work), sweep technicians, process servers, an office manager.
pf.staff.licenses: Each person's license or registration as pf.license says; a firearm permit for any armed work.
pf.staff.supervision: Unlicensed staff work only under the agency's license, where the state allows it.
pf.staff.who OKs: Sam, the licensed manager, reads every locate request and every new case before it books.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Only another licensed person with the skill, and the customer is asked first: a new person learns the case. Nobody moves on silence.

pf.rules.lawful purpose: Only lawful work; a protective order against the customer ends a locate.
pf.rules.no pretexting: Never get phone, bank or medical records by pretending to be someone (federal rules, as a switch).
pf.rules.tracking and recording: GPS tracking only on a car the customer owns, and recordings only where the state's consent rules allow (switches).
pf.rules.never police: Never poses as police, and never says or shows anything that looks like a badge.
pf.rules.license shown: The agency's license number on the listing, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.written contract: A signed client agreement before paid work, where the state's rules require it.
pf.rules.only where licensed: Work only in states where the agency is licensed.
pf.rules.records: As long as the state's rules require, at least 7 years; reports stay in the agency's own files.
pf.rules.status: Draft: finalized once the state forms are filled in.

matter most.the customer shares a phone or home with: Only the way the customer picks; no texts that name the work.
matter most.a locate request: Read by the licensed investigator first; a protective order ends it.
matter most.the person served avoids service: Up to 3 tries; more tries or a stake-out are priced first; never a no-show fee for the customer.
matter most.a device found in a sweep: Photographed and left; the customer decides about the police; told only on the secure page.
matter most.a serve-by date: Tries planned before it; if it can't be met, Sam calls the customer.

pf.edges.the rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

notes: Built on the sample plug-in (work/prof/private-investigator.json, test-drive Oct 25, verified: 10 findings, kept) with the lawyer's renames (law words changed to investigation words). Money: consult $100 (office, nothing taken; video card at DONE), home bug sweep $650 with a $325 deposit and the $325 rest billed, process serving $85 paid in full, client meeting $150 billed. The $100 fee is the late-cancel fee. The sample's off ops are kept; the lawyer's words ops are not copied (the sample had none). Not sure: the sweep's deposit and fee amounts; the $2 applies (D97). Licenses: none checked (D96).
